title: Support Operations Cost and Performance Analysis
executive_summary: Analysis of 220 support tickets reveals a total labor cost of $17,445.07. While overall satisfaction is high at 4.14, email support shows significantly higher reopening rates compared to chat. A small segment of high-cost, low-satisfaction tickets was identified, and ticket distribution across agents is relatively balanced.

key_findings.statement: The dataset contains 220 tickets with a mean resolution time of 75.66 minutes and a total labor cost of $17,445.07.
Team Beta incurred the highest labor cost at $6,928.72, followed by Gamma ($5,911.44) and Alpha ($4,604.91).
Chat channels have the longest mean resolution time at 82.23 minutes, followed by phone (74.07 minutes) and email (71.72 minutes).
The email reopen rate is 15.24%, which is 122.48% higher than the chat reopen rate of 6.85%.
There are 9 tickets in the high-cost, low-satisfaction segment, with a reopen percentage of 11.11%.
Resolution times have a median of 65.0 minutes and a standard deviation of 51.30 minutes. The mean satisfaction score is 4.14, with 14 missing satisfaction entries.
The team comprises 18 unique agents. The most active agent handled 16 tickets, representing 7.27% of the total volume.

limitations: The cleaning and analysis stages reported validation failures, suggesting potential data quality issues.
14 tickets are missing satisfaction scores, which may bias the satisfaction analysis.
The analysis assumes the 'reopened' flag accurately captures re-openings, dependent on the cleaning stage logic.
conclusion: Operational costs are driven by Team Beta and chat-based interactions. The significant increase in email reopen rates warrants investigation into email support processes. The high-cost, low-satisfaction segment, while small, represents a critical area for quality improvement.
